scope: WeakMap credential context, overwritten credentials, cross-client/server inspection, error provenance/path redaction
sanitization: Passed through the target's production Redactor.text to a fixed point. All example credentials, URLs carrying userinfo and query strings carrying credential values were removed and replaced by prose descriptions of their structure. No real credential was accessed at any point.

findings.title: Credential-shaped URLs are scrubled only in two narrow shapes, so config show/validate/serve --check-config can print a live credential verbatim
findings.evidence: Redactor.text has exactly two shape fallbacks (src/security.ts:17-22): URL userinfo that includes a password component, and query parameters named token, key, api-key-style or password. The loader only learns credential values from the three SECRET_KEYS (src/settings/load.ts:459-473) and from collectSecrets, which requires the assignment key to match /token|key|secret|password|credential/i (src/settings/load.ts:442-453). A credential held in git.ssh.push_url (schema-legal, src/config.ts:62,131) or client.url matches neither source and neither fallback: username-only userinfo and any other query name (access-token-style, header-style api-key, signature) survive verbatim.
findings.reproduction: Probe /tmp/rev38/probe/p2.ts with an empty secret set over eight placeholder inputs: the userinfo-with-password form was redacted; the username-only userinfo form was unchanged; the four recognised query names were redacted; the access-token-style, header-style api-key and signature query names were unchanged. Real CLI at target: swarmforge config show --config <throwaway>/s.toml (exit 0) printed the full client url value including its username-only userinfo and its access-token-style query value, with client.secrets reported as empty; swarmforge config validate --config <throwaway>/s.toml (exit 0) printed the full SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_URL value with its username-only userinfo intact.
findings.recommendation: During resolution, extract URL userinfo and credential-looking query values into collector.secrets so value-based redaction covers them on every surface, and broaden the two Redactor.text fallbacks to username-only userinfo and to any query key matching /token|key|secret|pass|auth|sig|credential/i.

findings.title: plain() keeps bidi overrides and zero-width characters, letting a hostile MCP endpoint spoof swarmforge status output
findings.evidence: plain() filters only C0 (below 0x20) and C1 (0x7f-0x9f); U+202E, U+202C and U+200B survive. Remote tool-error text is raised as an Error (src/cli/client.ts:45) and printed through scrub then redactedText then plain (src/cli.ts:121-132,184-186). src/security.ts:63-70 already strips exactly these code points for untrusted model output in excerptText, so the codebase treats them as dangerous elsewhere.
findings.reproduction: redactedText on a client result, given a message containing a right-to-left override, its terminator and a zero-width space, returned the string with all three code points intact (probe /tmp/rev38/probe/p1.ts, exit 0).
findings.recommendation: Reuse the isInvisible predicate from src/security.ts in plain(); it runs on already-redacted strings so widening it cannot affect redaction.
findings.confidence: high behaviour, low practical impact (requires a hostile or compromised endpoint)

findings.title: Serve and the running server rebuild a weaker secret set than the CLI, dropping the loader's all-layer credential context
findings.evidence: src/cli.ts:194,205 passes only settings.value to runServe, discarding the ResolvedSettings object that carries the WeakMap credentialContexts entry (src/settings/inspect.ts:14-22). commandRedactor builds its set from four resolved fields and redactorFor adds worker passwords, so superseded-layer credentials and credentials held in non-credential-named settings are unknown to serve logs, the event log (src/runtime.ts:172-212) and SSE/MCP payloads.
findings.reproduction: Code trace only. Every startup error path traced (src/providers/freestyle.ts:186-267, src/git-handoff.ts) raises fixed messages echoing neither the remote URL nor a token, and a superseded value is by construction not held by the serve process, so no trigger was demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Pass the recorded credential context into the serve process, or have commandRedactor/redactorFor accept it; at minimum add SWARMFORGE_GIT_PUSH_URL to redactorFor so the server matches the serve logger.

tests.command: Bun 1.4.2 (from /tmp/rev38/bun) in /tmp/rev38/t: bun test tests/inspect.test.ts tests/settings.test.ts -> 61 pass, 0 fail, 423 expects, exit 0; bun test tests/commands.test.ts -t config -> 6 pass, 9 filtered, 0 fail, 79 expects, exit 0; probes /tmp/rev38/probe/p1.ts,p2.ts,p3.ts and CLI config show / config validate -> exit 0
tests.note: Whole suite not run (whole-suite reviewer scope); packaging not compiled (packaging scope). No network, provider or real credential used.

limitations: Reviewed only the assigned scope; VM worker environment, adapters and packaging untouched.
F1 and F2 were reproduced locally with fake credential-shaped placeholders only; every literal has been replaced by prose in this sanitized export.
F3 is code-evidenced with no demonstrated trigger.

isServer surface confusion (src/settings/inspect.ts:35) checked and found unreachable: the server surface always resolves its host key (defaulted, src/config.ts:78) and the client value is exactly the url/token pair (src/settings/load.ts:891).
collectSecrets misses dotted TOML keys, but Bun.TOML.parse errors and zod strictObject issues echo no values, so no leak path was found there.
